title: SDK Pragmatics: Seamless Resumption, Adaptive Retries, and Stream Compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Product requirements for standardizing SDK behaviour across Python, TypeScript, and Go for pagination, retries, and streaming. This PRD formalizes: opaque resumable cursors, client-driven checkpointing for long-running streams, a single idempotency model for retryable calls, and a compatibility negotiation header so older SDKs gracefully downgrade to polling. The goal is to remove ad-hoc client implementations across libraries, reduce production incidents due to partial retries/resumes, and provide testable contracts for infra and SDK teams. Includes scope notes, rollout plan, and acceptance criteria.
scope_changes_and_rationale: Initial draft mandated server-managed cursor trimming and infinite server-side retention. After infra review (2026-03-04), we scoped this down: server will store opaque cursors for 7 days and expose cursor-expiry metadata; long-term resumption beyond 7 days will use client checkpointing to avoid unbounded state and reduce storage/ops burden. This change reduces infra cost and simplifies SLA guarantees.
requirements_summary: 1) Pagination: opaque cursor tokens, stable ordering guarantees, deterministic resume point; 2) Retries: unified idempotency token header, default exponential backoff with jitter, configurable max attempts per SDK; 3) Streaming APIs: windowed checkpoints within streams (checkpoint objects), explicit resume offsets, and backpressure signals via HTTP/2 or WS control frames; 4) Compatibility: feature-negotiation header, server-side graceful downgrade to polling endpoint, deprecation headers in responses.
python_interface_notes:
- sync iterator: client.paginate(...) yields Page objects with metadata {cursor, next_cursor, truncated} as attributes.
- async iterator: async for page in client.paginate_async(...): same semantics.
- resume: client.resume_from(cursor_token) factory accepts opaque token string.
- default retry policy: RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5, base_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=5s, jitter=true).
typescript_interface_notes:
- method signatures should return AsyncIterable<Page> and also provide .nextCursor() helpers.
- expose PollingFallback option: {streaming: true|false} decided during negotiation.
- idempotency: allow optional idempotencyKey parameter or auto-generate per-call with clear docs.
go_interface_notes:
- iterator pattern using channels: func Paginate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Page, <-chan error).
- resume: ResumeFrom(ctx, cursor string) returns same channel pair.
- concurrency: client-level MaxInflightPages config to control backpressure.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement opaque cursor tokens that can be serialized and used to resume a previously interrupted pagination/streaming session
Default retry policy enforced in SDKs and configurable by app; retries must include idempotency token header when provided
Streaming endpoints support in-band checkpoint records and a documented resume protocol that allows at-most-once re-delivery semantics for checkpointed segments
Compatibility header (X-Redwood-Client-Features) is present; server demonstrates graceful downgrade path to polling for at least two existing back-compat SDK versions
End-to-end integration tests in CI covering: interrupted stream resume, partial-page retry with idempotency token, and downgrade-to-polling behavior
Migration guide published with code examples for each language and a safety checklist for feature flags/rollouts
Performance regression: median pagination latency increase <= 5% and 95th percentile <= 10% compared to baseline for standard page sizes (256 tokens) when using resumeable flows
Telemetry events emitted for resume attempts, resume success/failure, retry attempts, and downgrade events with counts and sample traces
non_goals:
- Not implementing unlimited server-side cursor retention.
- Not changing model-level token pricing or tokenization semantics.
- Not introducing a new transport protocol beyond HTTP/2 and WebSocket for streaming in this phase.
rollout_plan: 1) SDK API review & acceptance tests (2 weeks) -> 2) Beta release of SDKs with feature-flagged resume and retries (opt-in) to 10% of customers (2 weeks) -> 3) Monitor telemetry and perf, iterate on thresholds (2 weeks) -> 4) Gradual enable by default with migration guide and deprecation notices (4 weeks).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Clients may misuse resume tokens leading to inconsistent reads. Mitigation: tokens are opaque and include server-side sequence/expiry; SDKs will expose helper methods to validate and refresh tokens. Risk: Increased operational load from resumed hot-shards. Mitigation: Cursor expiry and recommended client checkpoint frequency (default 15 minutes) distributed across routing buckets.
qa_and_test_requirements:
- Unit tests for cursor encode/decode compatibility across SDK versions.
- Integration tests that simulate network interruptions and verify resume correctness.
- Load tests for resume traffic patterns to validate infra limits.
- Fuzz tests for malformed cursor tokens.
- CI gating: all three SDKs must pass the resume/retry integration suite before feature-flag removal.
migration_notes: Provide CLI migration tool snippets: python example for converting offset-based loops to resumeable paginator; TS snippet demonstrating opt-in feature flag and fallback to polling. Include recommended logging level and observability spans for resume actions.
